questions.q: What distinguishes a real, documented risk acceptance from an unmanaged gap?
options: There is no real distinction — both mean the risk was never addressed
An acceptance must always be approved by an outside regulator
Acceptance can only apply to risks scored as Low

Acceptance is a documented decision, with sign-off from someone authorized to own the outcome, explaining why the cost of treating it exceeds the benefit — an unmanaged gap is a risk nobody ever decided about
questions.explain: A real acceptance is a tracked, authorized decision. A risk that just sat unaddressed because no one got to it isn't acceptance — it's an unmanaged gap, and auditors treat the two very differently.

questions.q: What does "mitigate" mean as a risk treatment option?
options: Reducing a risk's likelihood, its impact, or both, by implementing a control
Formally deciding to take no further action on the risk
Shifting the financial consequence of the risk to an insurer
Eliminating the activity that creates the risk entirely
questions.explain: Mitigation reduces likelihood and/or impact through a control, like rolling out hardware-key MFA or improving backup immutability — the default instinct for most security teams, though never free.

questions.q: What does risk transfer, such as cyber-insurance or a contractual indemnification clause, actually accomplish?
options: It eliminates the activity that creates the risk
It shifts the financial consequence of the risk to another party, without making the underlying risk disappear — and it has real limits like policy exclusions and payout caps
It reduces the likelihood of the risk occurring in the first place
It automatically removes the need for a risk register entry
questions.explain: Transfer shifts who pays, not whether the underlying exposure exists. Insurers exclude plenty of scenarios and cap payouts, and a vendor's indemnification is only as good as that vendor's ability to pay.

questions.q: What does "avoid" mean as a risk treatment, and why does it typically require a business decision-maker rather than just a security one?
options: Avoid means buying an insurance policy, which only a finance team can approve
Avoid means eliminating the activity or exposure that creates the risk entirely, which often conflicts directly with a business goal
Avoid means reducing the impact of a risk through a technical control
Avoid means accepting the risk but documenting it more thoroughly than usual
questions.explain: Avoidance removes the risk entirely — not launching a feature, decommissioning a legacy system, or exiting a jurisdiction — which is the most complete treatment but also the one most likely to collide with a business objective.

questions.q: What does a minimally complete risk register row need to include, according to this lesson?
options: Only the risk's name and the date it was first discovered
Only a qualitative High/Medium/Low label, nothing else
Only the name of the security engineer who first reported it
A description of the risk, its score or quantified loss exposure, its owner, the chosen treatment decision, specific actions/deadlines if mitigating, and a scheduled review date
questions.explain: Without those fields tracked in a register, a treatment decision is just a conversation that happened once in a meeting — easily forgotten, impossible to audit, and invisible to whoever inherits the risk later.
